title.narrative: Cash Consortium response to the drought crisis in ASAL region, Kenya

description.narrative: The project seeks to address food insecurity and livelihood loss for the most vulnerable drought -affected households in the counties of Marsabit, Mandera, Garissa, Wajir and Turkana. The project will provide multi -purpose cash assistance (MPCA) to 3,818 households over a period of 5 months (5 transfer cycles). The MPCA transfer values are based on the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), and for the populations in IPC3, the transfer values will be @50% of MEB, while for populations in IPC4, the transfer values will be @75% of MEB. The activities envisioned under this project include: (i) Selection, registration and verification of beneficiary households; (ii) Provision of emergency cash transfers to vulnerable households in drought -affected and food insecure areas: (iii) Monitoring and evaluation of the cash transfers; and, (iv)Review of Monthly complaints and feedback Mechanism (CRFM) reports and register. Similarly, the project seeks to support 574 flood affected households in Wajir with Multi -Purpose Cash Assistance for two cycles. The beneficiary HHs will receive cash which is equivalent to 50%MEB in Wajir. The beneficiaries will be selected using the following criteria: ? Households affected by floods: households that are displaced and living in camps/makeshift shelter whose property and livelihoods have been damaged or destroyed by the floods. ? Physiological vulnerability such as pregnant and lactating women, HHs with elderly members, children at risk, children with specific needs, people living with disabilities displaced by floods. ? Social vulnerability such as female -headed households, culturally segregated HHs, minority clans/groups/ethnic communities, unaccompanied and separated children displaced by flood. ? Economic vulnerability -HHs whose livelihoods has been destroyed by floods (e.g farms swept away, storage destroyed, livestock killed by floods)
